            for loop in range(minloop, maxloop+1):

report:
# Report on `region_004` (3,000 bp)

## Summary
The region is **not random sequence** — it is almost entirely occupied by **one long protein‑coding open reading frame (ORF)** on the **plus strand** whose product is a **P‑type cation‑transporting ATPase** (membrane pump). Nothing else notable (no repeats, no mobile elements, no low‑complexity or unusual regions) was found.

## General composition
| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Length | 3,000 bp |
| GC content | 52.1 % (uniform; no anomalous windows except a modest GC‑rich patch 1,101–1,200 ≈ 62 %) |
| Direct / inverted repeats (≥14 bp) | none |
| Tandem repeats / homopolymers | only trivial (e.g. A₆ at 1,470 and 2,181) |
| Predicted ORFs ≥ 40 aa | one dominant forward ORF; only short (≤205 aa) antisense artefacts elsewhere |

## Main feature — a single large ORF
- **Stop‑free reading frame:** plus strand, **nt 116 – 2,851** (no stop codons over 912 codons), terminated by a **stop codon TAA at nt 2,852 – 2,854**.
- **Likely CDS:** the first in‑frame **ATG is at nt 158 – 160**, preceded by a plausible ribosome‑binding site (**GGAGG‑like at nt ~145 – 149**, ~9 nt upstream). The ORF is preceded by a stop at 113–115.
- **Predicted protein:** **nt 158 – 2,851 = 2,694 bp = 898 amino acids** (M → … → Q).
- **Coding bias:** strongly enterobacterial/E. coli‑like (Leu almost exclusively CTG, Arg only CGT/CGC/CGG, no rare CGA/AGA/AGG; Ile mainly ATT/ATC), consistent with a genuine, probably reasonably expressed, gene.

## Protein identity — a P‑type ATPase
The 898‑aa product contains the complete diagnostic motif set of the **P‑type ATPase superfamily** (all coordinates 1‑based on the region):

| Motif (function) | aa | nt |
|---|---|---|
| **PEGL** (N‑domain) | 61–64 | 338–349 |
| **TGES** (A‑domain / phosphatase) | 213–216 | 794–805 |
| **DKTGTLT** (phosphorylation site) | 373–379 | 1,274–1,294 |
| **KGA** (A‑domain) | 468–470 | 1,559–1,567 |
| **TGD** (P‑domain) | 569–571 | 1,862–1,870 |
| **GDGIND** (ATP‑binding) | 640–645 | 2,075–2,092 |

Interpretation:
- The protein is a **polytopic membrane transporter**: the N‑terminal ~250 aa and the central ~350 aa (the actuator/nucleotide‑binding/phosphorylation domains) are hydrophilic, while the C‑terminal half carries several strongly hydrophobic segments (hydropathy peaks ≈ aa 719, 777, 845, 874; plus N‑terminal hydrophobic stretches ≈ aa 128, 248–330) — the expected transmembrane organisation of a P‑type ATPase.
- It carries **no CxxC or His‑rich metal‑binding motifs**, so it is not a Cu⁺/Zn²⁺‑type (P1B) pump. The size (≈898 aa) and motif layout fit the **MgtA‑type Mg²⁺‑transporting P‑type ATPases** (e.g. *E. coli* MgtA, 898 aa) most closely.

## Minor features
- **5′ flank (nt 1 – 157, upstream of the CDS):** 50.3 % GC; no recognisable promoter or secondary‑structure element.
- **3′ flank (nt 2,855 – 3,000, 146 nt):** 46.6 % GC; no further ORF.
- **3′‑terminal hairpin:** a short perfect inverted repeat at the extreme end, **5′‑CCTGAT‑(loop AGCGTAGCGCA)‑ATCAGG‑3′ (nt 2,978 – 3,000)**, i.e. a 6‑bp stem/11‑nt‑loop that could be the 5′ half of a Rho‑independent terminator extending past the supplied region.
- **Reverse strand:** no convincing gene; the longest antisense ORF (205 aa, plus‑strand coords ~1,736–2,352) overlaps the ATPase in the opposite frame and lacks a start/RBS context, so it is almost certainly spurious.

## Conclusion
The region **contains a complete gene, not "nothing"**: a single ~2.7‑kb ORF (nt 158 – 2,851, ≈898 aa; stop‑free frame 116 – 2,851) encoding a **P‑type ATPase membrane pump of the MgtA (Mg²⁺‑type) family**, with all canonical catalytic motifs present. Beyond this gene and a short 3′‑terminal hairpin, the sequence has no other notable features (no repeats, no mobile elements).
